coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED (in the order the task specified):
(1) Wikipedia team-season page — has the 12-row coaching-staff table plus explicit "Graduate assistants" and "Analysts" bullet lists. URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football_team
(2) rolltide.com's own archived-by-year 2020 staff page (still live): https://rolltide.com/sports/football/coaches/2020 — 11 coaches + 3 support staff only.
(3) THE KEY SOURCE: the Wayback capture of rolltide.com's full athletics staff directory from 25 Nov 2020 — mid-season, three weeks before the SEC title game: https://web.archive.org/web/20201125122240/https://rolltide.com/staff-directory . Its Football, Strength and Conditioning, Nutrition, Equipment, Athletic Training, Crimson Tide Productions, Video Operations, Communications, Photography and Academics sections give exact in-season titles for ~70 of the people below.
(4) The 2020 Alabama Football Media Guide (Internet Archive, https://archive.org/details/alabama-football-2020-media-guide), pp. 76-84, for people the web directory omits.

QUOTE CAVEAT — PLEASE READ. Every roster source here is a TABLE or a photo grid: the person's name and their title live in separate table cells (rolltide/Wayback) or separate text blocks (media guide). No contiguous run of page text contains "name + title" together. So the `quote` field holds the person's name exactly as that page renders it (verified by me as a literal substring of the extracted page text), and the exact title wording from the same row/grid cell is recorded in the `note` field and in the `role` field. I did not fabricate any combined name-plus-title string, because it would not string-match.

MEDIA-GUIDE-ONLY ROWS have quote:"" per your instruction. The media guide staff pages are a photo grid whose PDF text layer stores each name and each title as separate blocks; I reconstructed the pairings from the PDF's x/y coordinates (names row at one y, titles row directly beneath at matching x). That is reliable but not faithfully copyable as a quote. Affected: Gary Cramer, Brad Hill, Jessie Peoples, Kaleb Medena, and all 18 "Alabama Medical Staff" physicians/consultants.

WAYBACK FETCHABILITY: my own WebFetch tool is blocked from web.archive.org (curl works). If your verifier shares that limitation, the Wayback citations will fail to fetch even though they are correct. I therefore added a second, non-archive source (Wikipedia or the live rolltide 2020 page) to every person for whom one exists. ~35 people — most of the operations, video, graphics, nutrition, equipment and athletic-training staff — are documented ONLY by the Wayback directory and/or the media guide; there is no live non-archive page listing them.

MID-SEASON CHANGES (ring rule = on staff at the 11 Jan 2021 title game):
- Butch Jones DEPARTED. Hired as Arkansas State head coach 12 Dec 2020, before the SEC Championship Game and both CFP games. He is the one person below who was NOT on staff at the championship game. Flagged in midseason_note.
- Steve Sarkisian was named Texas head coach 2 Jan 2021 but stayed and called the offense in the title game — flagged, but he counts.
- Charles Huff (Marshall, 17 Jan), Kyle Flood and Jeff Banks (to Texas), Karl Scott (Vikings) all left AFTER the title game, so no note.
- Scott Cochran left for Georgia in Jan 2020, before the season, and is correctly absent.
- Freddie Roach and David Ballou/Matt Rhea all arrived before the season started (1st year), not mid-season.

WHAT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT:
- No "qc"/quality-control titles exist for Alabama in 2020 — the program used "Football Analyst" and "Graduate Assistant" instead, so the qc category is empty by design, not by omission.
- Student assistants, undergraduate managers, video interns and recruiting interns are NOT enumerated anywhere I could find. Alabama's directory and media guide both stop above that tier. There were certainly more such people; I did not guess at any.
- Rob Ezell is listed as an analyst by Wikipedia and the media guide grid but is absent from the 25 Nov 2020 web directory, so his in-season status rests on those two sources.
- Name-form discrepancies between sources (all the same person): Shiloh Keo (directory) vs "SHILOH KOE" (media guide OCR/typo); Michael vs Mike Stoops; AJ vs A. J. Milwee; Matthew vs Matt Clapp; Matthew vs Matt Hard; JT vs J.T. Summerford. I cited whichever spelling matches the URL given.
- INCLUSION JUDGEMENT YOU MAY WANT TO OVERRIDE: I included all 18 people the media guide lists under "Alabama Medical Staff" (pp. 83). Most are consulting physicians from Andrews Sports Medicine — team doctors, ophthalmologists, a radiologist, a chiropractor — not full-time football employees, and several serve all Alabama sports rather than football alone. They are genuinely documented team staff, so I did not drop them, but if your ring-counting rule is "employed by the football program," filter role_category=="medical" down to Jeff Allen, Bobby Feeback, Jeremy Gsell, Clay Keith, Ryan Vicknair and Ginger Gilmore-Childress, who the web directory confirms as football-assigned staff.
- Similarly, Amy Bragg, Kevin Murray, Molly Dowd, Kent Gidley, Daniel Lyerly and Gary Cramer are athletics-department-wide staff who appear in the FOOTBALL media guide's staff pages; I kept them for that reason and marked them "other".

Total: 96 people, every one carrying a real source. No names were added from memory or inference.
